2	
3	Base: 4a0eae2ea358038dc2d78818bc6dffdc946cfef0
4	Head: 9acd9c670dea38c1cffd8ca6d131835359da4562
5	
6	## Findings
7	
8	### 1. An expired or invalid invite stays in storage and keeps taking over the root
9	- Severity: Low
10	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:80, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:103, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:49
11	- What is wrong: The design says "The token is removed on every final outcome." The code removes it only after success, after already accepted, and on "Go back to your workspaces". `INVITE_EXPIRED` and `INVITE_NOT_FOUND` are final, because `inviteFailure` marks them not retryable, but `setFailure(outcome)` keeps the invite. To reach it, open an expired link and close the tab on the error card. For up to 30 minutes, each visit to `/m/` then goes to `/invite`, posts the dead token again, and shows the same card instead of the app. "Sign in with a different account" also keeps the dead invite, so the new account gets the same card after sign-in. Keeping the invite is correct only for `INVITE_EMAIL_MISMATCH` and for retryable failures.
12	- Smallest fix: Call `forgetInvite()` in the failure branch when the code is `INVITE_EXPIRED` or `INVITE_NOT_FOUND`. A `keepInvite` field on `InviteFailure` is enough to carry this. Otherwise, correct the sentence in the design.
13	
14	### 2. The questions-only path brings back the answers that `endOnboarding` just deleted
15	- Severity: Low
16	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:158, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:189, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/useDraftSave.ts
17	- What is wrong: On the last question, `reportCompleted` dispatches `completed`, and `onQuestionsDone` then calls `endOnboarding`, which clears the draft at once. The dispatch still re-renders, so the effect in `useDraftSave` queues the new draft. The timer or the flush on unmount then writes it back. Each new invited person who finishes the questions therefore keeps their answers in localStorage, although the `endOnboarding` comment says "its mark and answers go". The other exits do not have this problem, because no dispatch comes directly before the clear. The tests cannot catch it, because the host test mocks both `OnboardingFlow` and `endOnboarding`, and the flow test mocks `onQuestionsDone`. The stale draft is visible only if that person opens the onboarding page later, as a preview, so the harm is small.
18	- Smallest fix: Stop the draft save before the flow ends. For example, return a `stop` from `useDraftSave` that blocks later saves, and call it in the terminal branch of `advance`. Add one test with the real draft hook.
19	
20	### 3. A person who only answers questions can be blocked by a failure to set up an agent
21	- Severity: Low
22	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowScreen.tsx:24, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:71
23	- What is wrong: The invited flow never creates an agent, and the change turns off tool seeding for it for that reason. But `OnboardingFlowScreen` still calls `useEphemeralAgent(true)`, and `OnboardingFlowHost` still runs `useOnboardingModel`, the templates query and the connections query. If the mint fails, the invited person sees "Couldn't set up your agent" through `OnboardingFlowError` in place of the three questions, and gets no way to the project except the retry on that error. The mint comment says this happens when the user has not hydrated within its timeout. The new path therefore depends on work that it does not use.
24	- Smallest fix: In `OnboardingFlowScreen`, read the invited mark once the profile loads, and pass `false` to `useEphemeralAgent` for an invited account. At the least, do not render `OnboardingFlowError` for that account.
25	
26	### 4. The design says every string comes from the old page, but "Try again" does not
27	- Severity: Low
28	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/states/InviteAcceptError.tsx:26, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:87
29	- What is wrong: The settled rule is that the strings are copied from the old page to avoid invented copy, and the design states "Every string comes from the old page, so nothing is invented." `web/oss/src/pages/workspaces/accept.tsx` has no retry control and no "Try again" text. The retry itself is useful and the spec asks for it. The problem is that the document makes a claim that is false, so a reader does not know that this label and behavior are new.
30	- Smallest fix: Change the sentence in the design to say that the retry button is the one addition to the old page.
31	
32	### 5. Comments on the gate still say that invite links stay on desktop
33	- Severity: Low
34	- Where: web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:121, web/packages/agenta-shared/tests/unit/mobileGate.test.ts:46, web/packages/agenta-shared/tests/unit/mobileGate.test.ts:403
35	- What is wrong: This change makes `isTokenBearingAuthLink` and `isDesktopOnlyLink` return false for an invite link. The `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment still lists "any `/auth` link carrying a one-time token" as a route that finishes where it landed. Two test comments still say "SuperTokens password-reset and invite links carry a one-time ?token=" under the title "leaves a token-bearing auth link on desktop". A reader of this file gets the opposite of the new rule.
36	- Smallest fix: Add "other than an invite link" to the `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment, and remove "and invite" from the two test comments.
37	
38	### 6. The committed design points to a research note that is not in the repo
39	- Severity: Low
40	- Where: openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:3, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:33
41	- What is wrong: The design says "The full evidence is in the research note kept with the run", and it scopes out "side bugs in the research note". The change does not include that note, so a later reader cannot find the evidence or learn what those side bugs are.
42	- Smallest fix: Name the side bugs in the non-goals list, and delete the reference to the note.
43	
44	### 7. Nothing tests that Members opens the link dialog
45	- Severity: Low
46	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/settings/MembersTab.tsx:92, web/mobile/tests/unit/invitedLinkDialog.render.test.tsx
47	- What is wrong: The new tests render `InvitedLinkDialog` with its props only. The spec's two scenarios, a `{url}` response opens the dialog and a response without a link does not, live in the `onSuccess` branch of `MembersTab`, and no test runs that branch. If the branch breaks, the deployment with no email service silently loses its only way to share an invite, and the dialog tests still pass.
48	- Smallest fix: Add one `MembersTab` render test with a mocked `inviteToWorkspace` that resolves to `{url}` and then to `true`.
49	
50	## Rationale
51	
52	The main implementation is sound and follows the repo. I traced these paths and found no break in them: the password, one-time code and provider sign-in paths through `ContextResolver`, the signed-in visit to `/m/auth`, the gate order, and the question-only filter on `steps`. It reuses `onInvite`, `acceptWorkspaceInvite`, the pending-template storage shape and the projects query. Its tests assert real outcomes, including the StrictMode single accept and the Classic mode gates. No settled decision needs to be reopened. The live QA task, 7.2 in tasks.md, is still open, and I did not run the code.
53	
54	The two strongest reasons that the rating is not zero are both small state problems on new paths. A dead invite stays in storage and redirects the root for up to 30 minutes, which contradicts the design (finding 1). The questions-only exit writes the onboarding draft back after it was cleared, and it can also be blocked by a draft agent mint that it never uses (findings 2 and 3). Each of these needs a small fix and none weakens the core design.
55	
56	Rating: Low

1	You are a very strict reviewer of agent-generated code slop. Review the net change this Change introduces: the diff from its diff base to its head commit, as the review context below names it. Judge the code, not who wrote it.
2	
3	The subject of the review is the final state of the diff, not the commit history. Ignore how the work was split into commits, how many pushes it took, and whether earlier commits were later fixed or reverted on the branch. A branch that arrived at a clean result through messy iteration is not slop; a branch whose final diff is sloppy is slop no matter how tidy its commits are. Anything already at the diff base is existing code, not the subject of the review.
4	
5	Work from the review context:
6	
7	1. Start with the changed files and the patch in the review context. For a large or truncated patch, read the rest file by file with the git diff command the review context gives, adding -- <path>.
8	2. Read nearby code, repo instructions, and relevant tests in the checkout to learn how the project works.
9	3. You may skim the commit log from the diff base to the head commit to understand intent, but do not grade individual commits.
10	
11	Always review against the diff base the review context names, never the current tip of the base branch, so changes that landed on the base branch after the branch point are not attributed to this Change.
12	
13	This review is read-only against the repo's own tooling. Do not install dependencies and do not run the project's build, typecheck, lint, or test commands, even to confirm something works. Judge whether tests prove the new behavior by reading the test files and the code they exercise together, the same way you already read the diff. If a test's assertions don't match what the change claims to do, that is itself the finding.
14	
15	Do not use other AI agents or hand off the review. Do it yourself with the repo and local checks.
16	
17	Rate the amount of **Slop** the change adds as Low, Medium, or High. Slop is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repo well enough. It creates extra bugs, review work, or maintenance work.
18	
19	First understand what the change is trying to do. Follow every workflow, route, state change, and rule it touches from start to finish. Read whether the tests prove the new behavior instead of only matching the code or new text.
20	
21	Base the rating on:
22	
23	1. **Severity**: How much can the problem break or burden?
24	2. **Prevalence**: How much of the change has the problem?
25	3. **Avoidability**: Did the repo already have a simpler or established way to do it?
26	
27	Look for wrong assumptions, broken flows, skipped rules, duplicate systems, weak tests, needless complexity, comment noise (comments that restate the next line, narrate what was changed and why, or explain things the repo's conventions already make obvious), leftover debris from iteration (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches), and work that is much larger than the result it delivers. Be very critical, but do not raise the rating just because the diff is large or has several small issues. Do not call necessary complexity slop, and do not charge the change for problems it merely sits next to.
28	
29	Choose one:
30	- **Low** (signal value small): No real slop, or only small isolated issues that do not weaken the main implementation.
31	- **Medium** (signal value medium): A central wrong assumption, repeated low-trust work, weak checks for important behavior, or meaningful avoidable rework. The implementation can still be fixed without replacing its core.
32	- **High** (signal value large): Slop is widespread, the core approach is wrong or misleading, and much of it should be rewritten or removed.
33	
34	Report the rating as the signal. Its rationale must name the two strongest reasons for the rating, using concrete behavior or architecture problems, not surface-level signals. Report each concrete slop problem behind the rating as a finding anchored to the changed code it concerns.
35

1	# Slop review
2	
3	Base: 4a0eae2ea358038dc2d78818bc6dffdc946cfef0
4	Head: 9acd9c670dea38c1cffd8ca6d131835359da4562
5	
6	## Findings
7	
8	### 1. An expired or invalid invite stays in storage and keeps taking over the root
9	- Severity: Low
10	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:80, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:103, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:49
11	- What is wrong: The design says "The token is removed on every final outcome." The code removes it only after success, after already accepted, and on "Go back to your workspaces". `INVITE_EXPIRED` and `INVITE_NOT_FOUND` are final, because `inviteFailure` marks them not retryable, but `setFailure(outcome)` keeps the invite. To reach it, open an expired link and close the tab on the error card. For up to 30 minutes, each visit to `/m/` then goes to `/invite`, posts the dead token again, and shows the same card instead of the app. "Sign in with a different account" also keeps the dead invite, so the new account gets the same card after sign-in. Keeping the invite is correct only for `INVITE_EMAIL_MISMATCH` and for retryable failures.
12	- Smallest fix: Call `forgetInvite()` in the failure branch when the code is `INVITE_EXPIRED` or `INVITE_NOT_FOUND`. A `keepInvite` field on `InviteFailure` is enough to carry this. Otherwise, correct the sentence in the design.
13	
14	### 2. The questions-only path brings back the answers that `endOnboarding` just deleted
15	- Severity: Low
16	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:158, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:189, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/useDraftSave.ts
17	- What is wrong: On the last question, `reportCompleted` dispatches `completed`, and `onQuestionsDone` then calls `endOnboarding`, which clears the draft at once. The dispatch still re-renders, so the effect in `useDraftSave` queues the new draft. The timer or the flush on unmount then writes it back. Each new invited person who finishes the questions therefore keeps their answers in localStorage, although the `endOnboarding` comment says "its mark and answers go". The other exits do not have this problem, because no dispatch comes directly before the clear. The tests cannot catch it, because the host test mocks both `OnboardingFlow` and `endOnboarding`, and the flow test mocks `onQuestionsDone`. The stale draft is visible only if that person opens the onboarding page later, as a preview, so the harm is small.
18	- Smallest fix: Stop the draft save before the flow ends. For example, return a `stop` from `useDraftSave` that blocks later saves, and call it in the terminal branch of `advance`. Add one test with the real draft hook.
19	
20	### 3. A person who only answers questions can be blocked by a failure to set up an agent
21	- Severity: Low
22	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowScreen.tsx:24, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:71
23	- What is wrong: The invited flow never creates an agent, and the change turns off tool seeding for it for that reason. But `OnboardingFlowScreen` still calls `useEphemeralAgent(true)`, and `OnboardingFlowHost` still runs `useOnboardingModel`, the templates query and the connections query. If the mint fails, the invited person sees "Couldn't set up your agent" through `OnboardingFlowError` in place of the three questions, and gets no way to the project except the retry on that error. The mint comment says this happens when the user has not hydrated within its timeout. The new path therefore depends on work that it does not use.
24	- Smallest fix: In `OnboardingFlowScreen`, read the invited mark once the profile loads, and pass `false` to `useEphemeralAgent` for an invited account. At the least, do not render `OnboardingFlowError` for that account.
25	
26	### 4. The design says every string comes from the old page, but "Try again" does not
27	- Severity: Low
28	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/states/InviteAcceptError.tsx:26, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:87
29	- What is wrong: The settled rule is that the strings are copied from the old page to avoid invented copy, and the design states "Every string comes from the old page, so nothing is invented." `web/oss/src/pages/workspaces/accept.tsx` has no retry control and no "Try again" text. The retry itself is useful and the spec asks for it. The problem is that the document makes a claim that is false, so a reader does not know that this label and behavior are new.
30	- Smallest fix: Change the sentence in the design to say that the retry button is the one addition to the old page.
31	
32	### 5. Comments on the gate still say that invite links stay on desktop
33	- Severity: Low
34	- Where: web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:121, web/packages/agenta-shared/tests/unit/mobileGate.test.ts:46, web/packages/agenta-shared/tests/unit/mobileGate.test.ts:403
35	- What is wrong: This change makes `isTokenBearingAuthLink` and `isDesktopOnlyLink` return false for an invite link. The `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment still lists "any `/auth` link carrying a one-time token" as a route that finishes where it landed. Two test comments still say "SuperTokens password-reset and invite links carry a one-time ?token=" under the title "leaves a token-bearing auth link on desktop". A reader of this file gets the opposite of the new rule.
36	- Smallest fix: Add "other than an invite link" to the `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment, and remove "and invite" from the two test comments.
37	
38	### 6. The committed design points to a research note that is not in the repo
39	- Severity: Low
40	- Where: openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:3, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/design.md:33
41	- What is wrong: The design says "The full evidence is in the research note kept with the run", and it scopes out "side bugs in the research note". The change does not include that note, so a later reader cannot find the evidence or learn what those side bugs are.
42	- Smallest fix: Name the side bugs in the non-goals list, and delete the reference to the note.
43	
44	### 7. Nothing tests that Members opens the link dialog
45	- Severity: Low
46	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/settings/MembersTab.tsx:92, web/mobile/tests/unit/invitedLinkDialog.render.test.tsx
47	- What is wrong: The new tests render `InvitedLinkDialog` with its props only. The spec's two scenarios, a `{url}` response opens the dialog and a response without a link does not, live in the `onSuccess` branch of `MembersTab`, and no test runs that branch. If the branch breaks, the deployment with no email service silently loses its only way to share an invite, and the dialog tests still pass.
48	- Smallest fix: Add one `MembersTab` render test with a mocked `inviteToWorkspace` that resolves to `{url}` and then to `true`.
49	
50	## Rationale
51	
52	The main implementation is sound and follows the repo. I traced these paths and found no break in them: the password, one-time code and provider sign-in paths through `ContextResolver`, the signed-in visit to `/m/auth`, the gate order, and the question-only filter on `steps`. It reuses `onInvite`, `acceptWorkspaceInvite`, the pending-template storage shape and the projects query. Its tests assert real outcomes, including the StrictMode single accept and the Classic mode gates. No settled decision needs to be reopened. The live QA task, 7.2 in tasks.md, is still open, and I did not run the code.
53	
54	The two strongest reasons that the rating is not zero are both small state problems on new paths. A dead invite stays in storage and redirects the root for up to 30 minutes, which contradicts the design (finding 1). The questions-only exit writes the onboarding draft back after it was cleared, and it can also be blocked by a draft agent mint that it never uses (findings 2 and 3). Each of these needs a small fix and none weakens the core design.
55	
56	Rating: Low

15	- Severity: Medium
16	- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:78; web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:47
17	- What is wrong: The new path removes the agent steps but still opens `OnboardingFlowScreen`, which calls `useEphemeralAgent(true)`. A failed template fetch or model-candidate load makes that hook fail. The screen then replaces the questions with “Couldn't set up your agent.” The host also loads models, wallet data, templates, and tool connections that these users do not need. The added host test mocks these dependencies and does not cover the screen wrapper.
18	- Smallest fix: Select the invited flow before starting agent setup. Render the questions without the agent-specific hooks or setup error gate. Add a test that renders the invited route while agent setup services fail.
19	
20	## Rationale
21	
22	The change treats a failed profile read as permission to bypass the required onboarding decision. It also makes a survey depend on agent setup services, although invited users must not create an agent. These are concrete gaps in the main flow. Both can be fixed without replacing the invite implementation.
23

     2	
     3	All references are to `release/v0.127.3`.
     4	
     5	Today, an invited person takes this path:
     6	
     7	1. The email link is `<web_url>/auth?token&email&organization_id&workspace_id&project_id` (`organization_service.py:139-145`). The invite lasts 7 days (`:202`).
     8	2. `isDesktopOnlyLink` holds the link on the old app for every kind of user (`mobileGate/index.ts:343`).
     9	3. The old sign-in sends a new person to `/workspaces/accept?survey=true` and an existing person to `/workspaces/accept` (`web/oss/src/hooks/usePostAuthRedirect.ts:129-157`).
    10	4. The old accept page posts to the accept endpoint through `acceptWorkspaceInvite` (`web/packages/agenta-entities/src/organization/workspaceApi.ts:122-154`). On the cloud edition a new person then sees the `/post-signup` form, which sends `survey sent` (`web/ee/src/components/PostSignupForm/PostSignupForm.tsx:245`).
    11	
    12	On `/m` today:
    13	
    14	- `useSignInFlow` offers an `onInvite` callback for exactly this purpose (`web/packages/agenta-auth-ui/src/useSignInFlow.ts:157-163`), and `SignInScreen.tsx:49-56` does not pass it.
    15	- `useAuthSuccess` always goes to `/`, and a signed-in visit to `/auth` also goes to `/` (`features/app/authRoute.ts:19-27`).
    16	- `/` is `ContextResolver`, which forwards to a project home. It shows "No projects found." when the person has no project (`ContextResolver.tsx:98-103`).
    17	- A new account gets a pending onboarding mark. Home dismisses the mark when the project has agents, and otherwise starts the full flow (`onboardingPending.ts:70-82`).
    18	- The website `?template=` value already survives sign-in through localStorage with a 30 minute window (`lib/context.ts:29-70`).
    19	
    20	Password reset links are `<web_url>/auth/reset-password?token=...&tenantId=public` (`api/oss/src/core/auth/supertokens/config.py:70-73`). They carry `token` and never `organization_id`. `/m` has no reset screen.
    21	
    22	## Goals / Non-Goals
    23	
    24	Goals:
    25	
    26	- A new person and an existing person both join through `/m` from the emailed link, with every sign-in method.
    27	- A signed-in person with a different email sees the old page's mismatch message and can switch account.
    28	- An invite link already in an inbox keeps working.
    29	
    30	Non-goals:
    31	
    32	- Removing the old `/workspaces/accept` page. Nothing emails that URL (`organization_service.py` is the only link producer).
    33	
    34	## Decisions
    35	
    36	### Where the accept screen lives
    37	
    38	| Option | Trade-off |
    39	| --- | --- |
    40	| **`/m/invite`** | Outside `/auth`, so `authRedirectTarget` leaves a signed-in person there. |
    41	| `/m/auth/accept` | `isAuthRoute` would send a signed-in person to `/`, and `authRoute.ts` would need an exception. |
    42	| `/m/workspaces/accept` | Same path as the old page, but workspaces are being removed. |
    43	
    44	### How the invite survives sign-in
    45	
    46	| Option | Trade-off |
    47	| --- | --- |
    48	| **localStorage with a 30 minute window, written through `onInvite`** | The same shape as `?template=`. It survives a provider redirect. The token is removed on every final outcome. A mismatch keeps it, so the invited account can still use it. |
    49	| Carry the values in the OAuth state | It needs changes to the SuperTokens call and does nothing for password sign-in. |
    50	| A cookie | Sent to the server on every request, which a one-time token does not need. |
    51	
    52	A person who takes longer than 30 minutes opens the link again, because the link lasts 7 days.
    53	
    54	### Who sends the person to the accept screen
    55	
    56	| Option | Trade-off |
    57	| --- | --- |
    58	| **`ContextResolver`, before it resolves a project** | All sign-in paths and the signed-in visit end at `/`, so there is one reader. It also covers a person with no project yet. |
    59	| `useAuthSuccess` plus `OidcCallbackScreen` plus `authRoute` | Three places to keep in step. |
    60	
    61	### What the desktop gate tests
    62	
    63	| Option | Trade-off |
    64	| --- | --- |
    65	| **An invite link is an `/auth` link with both `token` and `organization_id`** | Reset links have no `organization_id`, so they keep today's route. |
    66	| Any `/auth?token=` | It would move reset links to `/m`, which has no reset screen. |
    67	
    68	The forward runs before the opt-out and Classic mode checks, and it keeps the query. `decideMobileGate` lets `/invite` and an invite link on `/auth` pass, because `desktopRouteFor` would drop the token.
    69	
    70	### Onboarding for a new invited person (Mahmoud chose questions only)
    71	
    72	| Option | Trade-off |
    73	| --- | --- |
    74	| **Questions only, then the invited project** | Keeps today's survey event. Needs a small path in onboarding. |
    75	| No questions | The least work. PostHog loses these answers. |
    76	| Leave `/m` as it is | No work. A viewer in an empty project gets steps written for an owner. |
    77	
    78	The accept screen adds an invited mark next to the pending mark and opens onboarding directly, so Home does not change. The onboarding host then shows only the question steps, sends the same events, ends onboarding after the last question, and opens the project home. It also skips seeding tool connections, because that belongs to setting up a new organization.
    79	
    80	### Invite link when email is off
    81	
    82	The API returns `{url}` when no email service is set up (`organization_service.py:295`), and `MembersTab.tsx` discarded it. `/m` now shows it in `InvitedLinkDialog`. Resending an invite stays out of scope, because `/m` has no resend action yet.
    83	
    84	### Wording
    85	
    86	The card strings come from the old page, and the Retry button uses the label `/m` already uses. `/m` cannot import `web/oss`, so the strings are copied into `features/invite/`. The page title "Accept invitation" is the one new string.
    87	
    88	## Risks / Trade-offs
    89	
    90	- A token sits in localStorage for up to 30 minutes. The old app also stores it there, with no window.
    91	- A shared browser: a second person who signs in within the window reaches the accept screen, and the API answers with the mismatch code. They see the error card, and "Go back to your workspaces" clears the invite.
    92	- A Helm install with the old web app turned off has no page for an old `/auth` link (`hosting/kubernetes/helm/tests/test_web_mobile.py:157`). The API change fixes new links, and old links expire within 7 days.
    93	- A Classic mode person who reloads `/m/` while the invite is pending goes to the old app. The next visit to the link finishes it.
    94	
    95	## Migration
    96	
    97	No data migration. Deploy order does not matter, because the old app forwards old links and the old app still exists for anything already in progress. Rollback restores the old link path, and any `/m/auth` invite link sent in the meantime still signs in, but it does not accept until the person opens a new invite.

     2	
     3	### Requirement: Invite link opens /m
     4	The API SHALL build the emailed invite link as `<web_url>/m/auth` with the same five query values as today.
     5	
     6	#### Scenario: Invite email is sent
     7	- **WHEN** an owner invites a person
     8	- **THEN** the link is `<web_url>/m/auth?token&email&organization_id&workspace_id&project_id`
     9	
    10	### Requirement: Invite survives sign-in
    11	The `/m` sign-in SHALL keep an invite that has a token and an organization id for 30 minutes in browser storage, through every sign-in method.
    12	
    13	#### Scenario: Password or one-time code
    14	- **WHEN** a person opens the link and signs in by password or one-time code
    15	- **THEN** `/m` opens the accept screen with the invite values
    16

     3	import {createEphemeralAppFromTemplate, fetchAgTypeSchema} from "@agenta/entities/workflow"

     5	import {queryClient} from "@/lib/queryClient"
     6	
     7	/**
     8	 * Mint the local-only agent that first run configures BEFORE it exists.
     9	 *
    10	 * The ephemeral is a real entry in the workflow molecule, so every entity-id-driven surface (the
    11	 * config pane, the model picker, the tools list) renders against it with no special casing. Only
    12	 * the two queries in `useAgentEntity` cannot resolve a `local-*` id, which is why the first-run
    13	 * screen passes this id in directly instead of letting the session resolve one.
    14	 *
    15	 * Deliberately NO abort-on-cleanup: React strict mode double-invokes effects (setup → cleanup →
    16	 * setup) and the ref guard blocks the second setup, so aborting on the first cleanup would cancel
    17	 * the only mint attempt and leave `entityId` null forever. The mint is client-only and cheap.
    18	 */
    19	/** The `x-ag-type-ref` the agent config node carries; see the seeding effect below. */
    20	const AGENT_TEMPLATE_AG_TYPE = "agent-template"
    21	
    22	export const useEphemeralAgent = (active: boolean) => {
    23	    const [entityId, setEntityId] = useState<string | null>(null)
    24	    /**
    25	     * Seed the `agent-template` type schema into the cache, under the same key
    26	     * `agTypeSchemaAtomFamily` reads.
    27	     *
    28	     * `parametersSchema` enriches every `x-ag-type-ref` node by merging in that type's schema, and
    29	     * the agent config IS such a ref. Its own query atom sits `pending` forever on this surface —
    30	     * mounted, but no request and no error — so the ref stays a bare stub
    31	     * (`type`, `x-ag-type-ref`, `title`, `description`, `default`) with no properties of its own.
    32	     * The config pane then has no fields to render and shows Advanced alone.
    33	     */
    34	    useEffect(() => {
    35	        // Through the cache, so it joins the schema atom's own request instead of racing it.
    36	        void queryClient
    37	            .ensureQueryData({
    38	                queryKey: ["workflows", "schemas", "ag-types", AGENT_TEMPLATE_AG_TYPE],
    39	                queryFn: () => fetchAgTypeSchema(AGENT_TEMPLATE_AG_TYPE),
    40	                staleTime: 5 * 60_000,
    41	            })
    42	            .catch(() => undefined)
    43	    }, [])
    44	
    45	    const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
    46	    const startedRef = useRef(false)
    47	
    48	    const mint = useCallback(() => {
    49	        if (startedRef.current) return
    50	        startedRef.current = true
    51	        setError(null)
    52	        void createEphemeralAppFromTemplate({
    53	            type: "agent",
    54	            defaultName: "New agent",
    55	            // NOT `deferInspect`. The config pane is the point of this surface, and its Model,
    56	            // Instructions, Tools and Skills sections are schema-driven — deferring the inspect
    57	            // renders a pane with only Advanced and Triggers in it. Nothing here subscribes to the
    58	            // readiness atoms that drive the resolution, so the mint waits for the schema it is
    59	            // about to display.
    60	        })
    61	            .then((id) => {
    62	                if (!id) throw new Error("mint returned no entity id")
    63	                setEntityId(id)
    64	            })
    65	            .catch(() => {
    66	                // Release the guard so `retry` can re-run. The mint gives up when the signed-in
    67	                // user has not hydrated within its own timeout, which is recoverable — never
    68	                // leave the surface spinning on it.
    69	                startedRef.current = false
    70	                setError("Couldn't set up your agent.")
    71	            })
    72	    }, [])
    73	
    74	    useEffect(() => {
    75	        if (!active) return
    76	        mint()
    77	    }, [active, mint])
    78	
    79	    return {entityId, error, retry: mint}
    80	}

const AUTH_RE = /^\/auth(\/|$)/

const INVITE_ROUTE_RE = /^\/invite\/?$/

/** An emailed invite: `/auth` with a one-time token and its organization. A reset link has neither the path nor the organization. */
export function isInviteLink(pathname: string, search: string): boolean {
    if (!/^\/auth\/?$/.test(pathname)) return false
    const params = new URLSearchParams(search)
    return Boolean(params.get("token") && params.get("organization_id"))
}

/**
 * An `/auth` link carrying a one-time `token` (SuperTokens password reset) completes on desktop.
 * The desktop gate forwards an invite link before it reaches this check.
 *
 * Redirecting it would drop the token twice over: `mapDesktopToMobile` returns a bare `/m/auth`,
 * and the mobile app has no screen that consumes one. Same reasoning as the OAuth callback
 * exception — a single-use credential must not be bounced.
 */
export function isTokenBearingAuthLink(pathname: string, search: string): boolean {
    if (!AUTH_RE.test(pathname)) return false
    return Boolean(new URLSearchParams(search).get("token"))
}

/**
 * An `/auth` link carrying `auth_error` completes on desktop, for the same reason as a token: the
 * param IS the payload. `web/oss/src/lib/api/assets/axiosConfig.ts` redirects a 403 here so the
 * user can finish required SSO or social re-authentication, and the desktop auth page reads it.
 * `mapDesktopToMobile` returns a bare `/m/auth`, so redirecting would drop the reason and leave
 * the user on a sign-in screen that cannot explain why it appeared.
 */
export function isPolicyAuthLink(pathname: string, search: string): boolean {
    if (!AUTH_RE.test(pathname)) return false
    return Boolean(new URLSearchParams(search).get("auth_error"))
}

    if (DESKTOP_EXCEPTIONS.some((re) => re.test(pathname))) return true

## Why

Invite emails open the old app. `api/oss/src/services/organization_service.py:139-145` builds `<web_url>/auth?token=...`, `isTokenBearingAuthLink` keeps that link on the old sign-in, and the person accepts on the old `/workspaces/accept` page. `/m` is the main app, and it drops every invite value except `email` during sign-in.

## What Changes

- The API builds the invite link with `/m/auth`.
- The `/m` sign-in keeps the invite in browser storage through password, one-time code, social and SSO sign-in.
- `/m` gets an accept screen at `/m/invite`, with the outcomes of the old page.
- The person lands in the invited project.
- A new invited person answers the onboarding questions only, then opens the invited project.
- The desktop gate forwards an old invite link to `/m/auth` with its query. Password reset links stay where they are.
- The mobile gate does not send an invite away from `/m` for a Classic mode user.
- `/m` Members settings shows the invite link when the deployment has no email service.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `mobile-invites`: joining an organization from an emailed invite link in `/m`.

### Modified Capabilities

None. No existing spec covers invites.

## Impact

- `api/oss/src/services/organization_service.py`: link path only. No API contract change.
- `web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts` and its tests.
- `web/mobile/src/features/invite/` (new), `web/mobile/src/pages/invite/index.tsx` (new), `SignInScreen.tsx`, `ContextResolver.tsx`, `features/onboarding/*`.
- `docs/design/onboarding-revamp/questions-and-survey-parity.md`: the old form no longer sends `survey sent` for invites.
- No change to `web/oss` or `web/ee`, which are abandoned.

# Slop review

Base: 4a0eae2ea358038dc2d78818bc6dffdc946cfef0
Head: 1b8d1f25d7de993240d1d6948d7cf80978c1b7fb

## Findings

### 1. The post-auth loader covers the invite error card for up to 20 seconds
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/InviteAcceptScreen.tsx:4, web/mobile/src/features/invite/InviteAcceptScreen.tsx:7, web/mobile/src/features/app/BootLoaderScreen.tsx:56, web/mobile/src/features/app/BootLoaderScreen.tsx:78, web/mobile/src/features/app/postAuthBoot.ts:42
- What is wrong: `useAuthSuccess` raises `PostAuthLoader`, a fixed overlay at `z-[100]`, on every sign-in. `BootLoaderScreen` leaves at stage 2 or after `BOOT_MAX_MS`, which is 20 seconds. When the person has at least one project, stage 2 needs `Boolean(projectId) && !agents.isPending`. `/invite` has no project in its route, so `ContextSync` keeps `projectIdAtom` null, and the loader stays at stage 1. On the success path this does no harm, because `openProject` moves to a project route. On a failure, `/invite` is the last route, so the card renders under the overlay. To reach it, open an expired link, or a link for another email, and sign in with an account that has a project. The person sees "Loading your agents" for 20 seconds, and only then sees the message and the buttons. The same wait applies to the new failed profile read. The mismatch and expired scenarios in the spec are therefore late for a person who signs in from the link. A signed-in visit raises no loader and does not have this wait. The comment on line 4 names the loader for the accepting state, but nothing handles the failure state. `useInviteAccept.render.test.tsx` renders the screen without `PostAuthLoader`, so the tests cannot catch this. I found this by reading the code. I did not run it, so live QA task 7.2 should confirm it.
- Smallest fix: Clear the loader when a failure is set, for example `setBoot(null)` with `useSetAtom(postAuthBootAtom)` in `useInviteAccept`, in the same place as `setFailure`. Add one test that asserts the atom is null after a failed accept.

### 2. No test covers the fix that stops agent setup on the questions-only path
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowScreen.tsx:26, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowScreen.tsx:27
- What is wrong: Round 1 raised that a failed mint blocks an invited person, and the fix is the changed argument to `useEphemeralAgent`. No test renders `OnboardingFlowScreen`. The host test mocks the flow and starts below this screen, so it does not cover the gate. If a later edit restores the mint, or changes the `isPending` condition, the invited person can again get "Couldn't set up your agent" in place of the questions, and every test still passes. The change also moves the start of the mint for ordinary new accounts until the profile has loaded, and no test covers that either. This is not the deferred `MembersTab` item.
- Smallest fix: Add one render test for `OnboardingFlowScreen` with a mocked `useEphemeralAgent`. Assert that it gets `false` for an invited user and `true` for a user with no invited mark.

### 3. Two checked tasks and one gate comment still describe what the fix removed
- Severity: Low
- Where: openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/tasks.md:7, openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/tasks.md:22, web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:121
- What is wrong: The fix commit corrected the design and the spec, but not `tasks.md`. Task 2.1 is checked and says "exclude it from `isTokenBearingAuthLink`", but that exclusion is gone. Task 4.3 is checked and says "write the last context", but `useInviteAccept` no longer does this. Also, the `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment still says that routes in its list "finish where they landed, whatever any gate would prefer", and it lists any `/auth` link with a one-time token. An invite link matches that function and `decideDesktopGate` forwards it first. The new note on `isTokenBearingAuthLink` is correct, but a reader of the list comment does not see it.
- Smallest fix: Change task 2.1 to "forward it before the `isDesktopOnlyLink` check". Change task 4.3 to say that `ContextSync` writes the last context. Add "except an invite link, which the desktop gate forwards first" to the `isDesktopOnlyLink` comment.

## Rationale

The first reason is that a failure outcome of the new accept screen is hidden behind the post-auth loader for a person who signs in from the link and has a project (finding 1). The second reason is that the fix for the questions-only path has no test at the screen where the fix lives (finding 2). Both are isolated and need small changes, and neither weakens the main implementation, so the rating stays Low even though finding 1 should be fixed before merge.

I checked the round 1 fixes by reading the code, and these are correct and complete:
- The profile read now comes before the accept, and a failed read or a null profile keeps the invite and offers Retry. The test proves this. A failed read is not cached, so Retry reads again.
- `keepInvite` clears the invite on expired, not found and already accepted. It keeps the invite on a mismatch and on an unknown failure. This matches the design and the spec, and the test covers both codes.
- The invited mark is set only when the pending mark stands, and `clearOnboardingPending` removes both. So the invited check in `OnboardingFlowScreen` cannot disagree with the one in `OnboardingFlowHost`. The screen re-reads the mark on each render, but after `endOnboarding` a re-render before the route change would only start a local mint, so I did not raise it.
- The hooks that stay in the host for an invited person (model, wallet, templates, connections) do not gate the question steps, so a failure there does not block the questions. With a null `entityId` the host works as it does during a mint.
- Removing the `isInviteLink` check from `isTokenBearingAuthLink` is safe. `decideDesktopGate` forwards first, and `useClassicModeRedirect`, the only other caller of `isDesktopOnlyLink`, returns earlier for `/auth`.
- Removing the bare 409 branch is correct. The accept route sends a 409 only with the `INVITE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED` code.
- Removing `writeLastContext` is correct. `ContextSync` writes it on every route with a workspace and a project, including the onboarding route.
- "Retry" is the label `ContextResolver` already uses, and the design sentence on wording is now true.

`if (outcome.alreadyAccepted && user)` has a `user` check that is never false at run time. It exists only for the type, and it does no harm, so I did not raise it. I did not raise rejected or deferred items again.

Rating: Low
